BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r4.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether earlier generations advised later ones to use the same slur, marveling that the accusation recurred across eras.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r4.anchor: إنكار وتعجيب من حالهم وإجماعهم على تفرق أزمانهم على تلك الكلمة الشنيعة

BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r5.claim: He rejects mutual advice as the explanation because the generations were separated; their shared insult instead arose from each group’s innate transgression and wicked disposition.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r5.anchor: إضراب عن كون مدار اتفاقهم على الشر تواصيهم بذلك لبعد الزمان وعدم تلاقيهم

BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.claim: Inwardly, rebellious souls in every age share a satanic nature of refusal, pride, and defiance, so they reject outward prophets and inward divine inspirations alike as magic or madness; abundance, comfort, arrogance, and wealth feed their transgression.
BURSEVI:v9p141#2/r6.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أن أرباب النفوس المتمردة من الأولين والآخرين مركوزة في جبلتهم طبيعة الشيطنة من التمرد

MAJAZ:v2p227/r1.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p227/r1.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p227/r1.claim: أتواصوا به means they mutually agreed on it or took it from one another; a dominant shared trait can seem as if a people advised one another to it.

NAHHAS:v4p249/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p249/r12.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether one generation instructed another to say this.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r12.anchor: أي هل أوصى بعضهم بعضا بهذا

NAHHAS:v4p249/r13.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p249/r13.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p249/r13.claim: They did not coordinate; they are a tyrannical people who overstep and disobey God’s commands and prohibitions.
NAHHAS:v4p249/r13.anchor: بل هم قوم طغوا واعتدوا فخالفوا أمر الله جل وعز ونهيه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r1.claim: The question expresses wonder that disbelievers of separated eras converge on rejecting prophets; they did not conspire but acted as if they had.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى: أتواصوا به توقيف وتعجيب من توارد نفوس الكفرة في تكذيب الأنبياء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r2.claim: Their common cause is tyranny; a tyrant is arrogant on earth, corrupting and defiant toward God.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p182/r2.anchor: والعلة في ذلك أن جميعهم طاغ، والطاغي: المستعلي في الأرض المفسد العاتي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r1.claim: “Did they instruct one another?” is a rebuke: did earlier and later people pass this accusation along to one another?
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r1.anchor: أي أوصى أولهم آخرهم بالتكذيب وهذا استفهام توبيخ

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r2.speaker: أبو عبيدة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r2.claim: Abū ʿUbayda reads the question as asking whether they colluded in it and copied the accusation from one another.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r2.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة أتواطؤوا عليه فأخذه بعضهم من بعض

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r3.claim: The people addressed are the Meccans; their transgression in the worldly goods given to them drives their denial.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p42#2/r3.anchor: أي يحملهم الطغيان فيا أعطوا من الدنيا على التكذيب والمشار إليهم أهل مكة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r2.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether opponents passed the accusation to one another; rather they are rebellious, with later hearts resembling earlier ones.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p425/r2.anchor: أوصى بعضهم بعضا بهذه المقالة؟ " {بل هم قوم طاغون}

JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.claim: The narratives of earlier communities provide lessons for anyone who reflects; this is why they are recounted.
JISHUMI:v9p6599/r1.anchor: وتدل على أن في قصصهم عبرة لمن تدبر، وأنه إنما ذكر ليعتبر به

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r1.claim: The pronoun refers to the accusation: did generations advise each other to repeat this identical charge?
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r1.anchor: الضميرللفول اى اتواصى الاولون والاخرون بهذا القول حتى قالوه جميعا

NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r2.claim: They did not coordinate because they lived at different times; the shared cause is transgression, which drives them to say it.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p181#9/r2.anchor: لم يتواصوا به لانهم لم يتلاقوا في زمان واحد بل جمعتهم العلة الواحدة وهى الطغيان

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r16.claim: The question asks if earlier generations advised later ones to make the same accusation; its alif conveys rebuke and astonishment.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r16.anchor: { أتواصوا به } أي أوصى أولهم آخرهم بالتكذيب. وتواطأوا عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r17.claim: They did not conspire; their shared excess in disbelief explains the repeated charge.
QURTUBI-FULL:51:50-55/r17.anchor: أي لم يوص بعضهم بعضا بل جمعهم الطغيان، وهو مجاوزة الحد في الكفر.

RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r1.claim: “Did they counsel one another?” expresses wonder that all peoples used the same charge, as if they had agreed to say only that messengers were sorcerers or mad.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r1.anchor: أي كيف اتفقوا على قول واحد كأنهم تواطؤا عليه

RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r2.claim: Rāzī denies actual collusion: shared affluence made them self-sufficient, forgetful of God, and transgressive, so they rejected their messengers.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r2.anchor: لم يكن ذلك على التواطؤ ، وإنما كان لمعنى جامع

RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r3.claim: He compares them to subjects whom a king leaves unburdened until they build luxurious estates; when summoned later, they find obedience difficult and turn to another ruler.
RAZI-FULL:v28p197#3/r3.anchor: إذا أمهل أهل بقعة ، ولم يكلفهم بشيء

STUDYQURAN:51:53/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r1.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r1.claim: The question can mean that they urge one another to call the Prophet a sorcerer or possessed, and thus to deny him.
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r1.anchor: exhort one another to saying that the Prophet is a sorcerer or one possessed (R)

STUDYQURAN:51:53/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r2.speaker: Most commentators
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r2.claim: They read the question with wonder: would the people really urge one another to deny God and revelation?
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r2.anchor: Most commentators interpret this verse as an expression of wonder that they would in fact exhort one another to denial

STUDYQURAN:51:53/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r3.speaker: Āl
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r3.claim: Alternatively, the question may be a negation: they do not exhort one another to it, with “it” referring to belief.
STUDYQURAN:51:53/r3.anchor: it could also be understood as a negation meaning, “They do not exhort one another to it” (Āl)

TAB-FULL:v21p550/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p550/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p550/r1.claim: Just as Quraysh called Muhammad a poet, sorcerer, or madman, earlier peoples who were punished—Noah's people, ʿAd, Thamud, and Pharaoh's people—called their messengers sorcerers or madmen.
TAB-FULL:v21p550/r1.anchor: كقوم نوح وعاد وثمود، وفرعون وقومه

TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r1.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether Quraysh inherited an instruction from earlier generations to reject Muhammad; their agreement instead reflects that they are all rebellious.
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة، {أتواصوا به بل هم قوم طاغون} [الذاريات: 53] قال: «أوصى أولاهم أخراهم بالتكذيب»

TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r2.claim: Qatada says earlier generations instructed later ones to deny the truth.
TAB-FULL:v21p550#2/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أتواصوا به} [الذاريات: 53] «أي كان الأول قد أوصى الآخر بالتكذيب»

ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r1.claim: The first people advised the last to say the same thing; the opening hamza is both reproach and interrogation.
ZAJJAJ:v5p58/r1.anchor: معناه أوصى أولهم آخرهم، وهذه ألف التوبيخ وألف الاستفهام

TABATABAI:51:52-56/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r4.claim: Mutual enjoining is a people's advising one another; the pronoun refers to the accusation. The amazed question asks whether earlier and later peoples advised each other to say it; rather, their transgression drives the charge.
TABATABAI:51:52-56/r4.anchor: للقول، والاستفهام للتعجيب، والمعنى هل وصى بعض هذه الأمم بعضا

TABRISI:51:52-57/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:51:52-57/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:51:52-57/r2.claim: “Did they advise one another?” is a rebuke: they did not conspire across generations but shared tyranny, emboldened by abundance to reject prophets.
TABRISI:51:52-57/r2.anchor: معناه لم يتواصوا بذلك لكنهم طاغون طغوا في معصية الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r1.claim: Ataṣāwaw bihi means whether they instructed one another to use this accusation.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r2.speaker: مقاتل
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r2.claim: Muqātil says earlier people instructed later people to say this about their messenger.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r2.anchor: يعني أوصى الأول الآخر يقول ذلك لرسوله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r3.speaker: قتادة
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r3.claim: Qatāda says the earlier generations instructed later ones to deny the messenger.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r4.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r4.claim: Al-Zajjāj says the initial hamza is interrogative and rebuking.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says their transgression in the prosperity God gave them led them to deny the Prophet.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r5.anchor: حملهم الطغيان فيما أعطيتهم ووسعت عليهم على تكذيبك

WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r6.claim: The question is answered no: they were not advised by their predecessors but were people who exceeded bounds in disobedience.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v20p464/r6.anchor: والمعنى ما أوصى أولهم بذلك، ولكنهم قوم خارجون عن الحد في العصيان

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:51:52-58/r2.claim: “Did they advise one another?” is a rebuke implying that some instructed others to disbelieve; rather, they are transgressors.

ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r2.speaker: Asad
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r2.claim: He frames the charge as inherited thinking, then explains the rejection as the people's overweening arrogance.
ASAD-NOTES:51:52/r2.anchor: perchance, handed down this [way of thinking] as a legacy unto one another? Nay

ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:51:47-60#2/r16.claim: The question whether they advised one another is rhetorical: many had no knowledge of one another, yet their transgression made their accusations alike.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r5.claim: The passage raises and rejects the idea that accusations were inherited culturally from earlier peoples, then identifies shared transgression as the cause, driven by prejudice and stubborn denial.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r5.anchor: asıl sebebin öncekilerle bunların “azgınlık, taşkınlık etme” şeklinde özetlenebilecek ortak bir özellik taşımaları olduğu belirtilmektedir

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r6.speaker: Taberî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r6.claim: Tabari understands the opening as asking whether this belief was passed from generation to generation.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r6.anchor: “Bu, nesilden nesile aktarılan bir telakki mi?” şeklinde anlarken

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r7.speaker: müfessirlerin çoğu
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r7.claim: Most exegetes read it as sarcastic astonishment: the separated generations could not have influenced one another directly.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r7.anchor: hayretle karışık bir istihzâ ifadesi olarak kabul edip aynı zaman diliminde yaşamadıkları için böyle bir etkileşimin imkânsız olduğu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r8.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r8.claim: The author translates the line as if generations had advised one another of the accusation, then clarifies that they are a transgressive people.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:51:52/r8.anchor: “Sanki nesiller boyu birbirlerine hep bunu tavsiye etmişler! Daha doğrusu onlar azgın bir topluluk!”

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.claim: Every nation treated its messenger similarly, so the Prophet should patiently continue, turn from wrongdoers, and remind those who respond; God will support him and his companions.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p515/r2.anchor: the same attitude was adopted by every nation towards their respective messengers

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r4.claim: The author expresses amazement that every generation seems to pass down a will instructing its successors to oppose messengers in the same way.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r4.anchor: it is as if the miscreants of every nation have made a will to the ones who will come later

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r5.claim: The real cause of the Quraysh’s similarity to earlier rejecters is their shared rebellious character, which leads them to the same fate.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-7-english:p519/r5.anchor: the real cause of this similarity in attitude is that these people [the Quraysh] also are rebellious

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p245#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p245#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p245#4/r1.claim: Qatada explains ‘Did they pass it down to one another?’ as meaning that earlier generations instructed later ones to lie.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p245#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ أتواصوا به ﴾ قال يقول أوصى أولهم آخرهم بالكذب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r9.claim: أتواصوا به expresses amazement that people in separated eras repeated the charge; they shared transgression and arrogance, not conspiracy.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v9p560/r9.anchor: وهو توقيف وتعجيب من توارد نفوس الكفرة على تكذيب الأنبياء،

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r1.claim: The question marvels that earlier and later rejecters all used the same vile accusation, as if they had advised each other to say it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r1.anchor: تعجيب من إجماعهم على تلك الكلمة الشنيعة أي كأن الأولين والآخرين منهم أوصى بعضهم بعضا

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r2.claim: Alternatively, the question denies that they ever conspired together to say it.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r2.anchor: وقيل : إنكار للتواصي أي ما تواصوا به

ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r3.claim: The “rather” clause redirects from shared counsel to their actual common cause: participation in transgression that drives the accusation.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p19#2/r3.anchor: إضراب عن أن التواصي جامعهم إلى أن الجامع لهم على ذلك القول مشاركتهم في الطغيان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r1.claim: The question asks whether earlier and later opponents advised one another to deny the message; its opening alif is reproachful.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r1.anchor: أي: أوصى أولهم آخرهم وبعضهم بعضا بالتكذيب وتواطؤا عليه؟ والألف فيه للتوبيخ،

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says their rebellion over God's gifts and abundance drove them to deny the Prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p380/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: حملهم الطغيان فيما أعطيتهم ووسعت عليهم على تكذيبك،

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r3.claim: The question pictures earlier and later peoples as if they had passed the same accusation to each other; the author says shared tyranny, not actual cross-generational counsel, explains it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r3.anchor: كأن الأولين والآخرين منهم أوصى بعضهم بعضا بهذا القول

BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r4.claim: The author rejects actual counsel because those generations were far apart in time; their shared tyranny prompted the accusation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:51:52-54/r4.anchor: الجامع لهم على هذا القول مشاركتهم في الطغيان

BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r3.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether generations conspired to repeat the charge; they did not meet, but shared the trait of rebellious excess.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r3.anchor: لأن الأولين ما اجتمعوا مع الآخرين : { بل هم } اجتمعوا في وصف

BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r4.claim: The rebellious are proud, excessive in unbelief, wrongdoing, and disobedience; the pronoun suggests transgression is ingrained in them, and God brings them to ruin through complete power and knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p287/r4.anchor: عالون في الكفر مسرفون في الظلم والمعاصي مجاوزون للمقدار

BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.speaker: أبو جعفر بن الزبير
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.claim: The question whether deniers taught one another their stance or are simply transgressive points to arrogance and darkened hearts as the common cause of their disbelief; God could have guided every soul.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p271#2/r5.anchor: أي عجبا لهم يف جريهم على التكذيب والفساد

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r1.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r1.claim: Avicenna defines sound as a quality arising from undulating air compressed between an impacting and an impacted body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r1.anchor: ذكر الرئيس أبو علي بن سينا في تعريف الصوت أنه كيفية تحدث من تموج الهواء المنضغط بين قارع ومقروع

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r2.claim: Razi says sound is known directly by hearing; Avicenna's account, if accepted, describes its cause rather than its essence.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r2.anchor: ماهية الصوت مدركة بحس السمع وليس في الوجود شيء أظهر من المحسوس حتى يعرف المحسوس به

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r3.speaker: النظام
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r3.claim: Al-Naẓẓām is said to have held that sound is a body.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r3.anchor: يقال إن النظام المتكلم كان يزعم أن الصوت جسم

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r4.claim: The arguments against identifying sound with body are that bodies share corporeality but not sound, are visible and tangible unlike sound, and persist while sound does not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r4.anchor: منها أن الأجسام مشتركة في الجسمية وغير مشتركة في الصوت ومنها أن الأجسام مبصرة وملموسة أولا وثانيا وليس الصوت كذلك

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r5.claim: Razi doubts that the intelligent al-Naẓẓām equated sound itself with body; he likely said air undulation causes sound, which people misconstrued.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r5.anchor: وأقول : النظام كان من أذكياء الناس ويبعد أن يكون مذهبه أن الصوت نفس الجسم

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r6.speaker: بعضهم
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r6.claim: Some define sound as the collision of solid bodies, but Razi rejects this because collision is visible contact whereas sound is not visible.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم : الصوت اصطكاك الأجسام الصلبة وهو باطل ؛ لأن الاصطكاك عبارة عن المماسة وهي مبصرة

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r7.claim: Other proposed definitions identify sound with impact, tearing apart, or motion's undulation; Razi rejects them because those states are visible and sound is not.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r7.anchor: وقيل : الصوت نفس القرع أو القلع وقيل أنه تموج الحركة وكل ذلك باطل

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r8.claim: Sound's proximate cause is an air undulation, not a single movement traveling from one fixed starting point to one fixed endpoint; it unfolds through successive impacts and pauses.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r8.anchor: ولا نعني بالتموج حركة انتقالية من مبدأ واحد بعينه إلى منتهى واحد بعينه بل حالة شبيهة بتموج الهواء

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r9.claim: The undulation is caused by forceful contact, called impact, or forceful separation, called tearing; Razi directs readers to his rational works for the nature of the phoneme.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r9.anchor: وأما سبب التموج فإمساس عنيف وهو القرع أو تفريق عنيف وهو القلع

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r10.speaker: أبو علي بن سينا
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r10.claim: Avicenna defines a letter as a quality of sound that distinguishes it perceptibly from another sound of the same lightness or heaviness.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r10.anchor: قال الشيخ الرئيس في حد الحرف : إنه هيئة عارضة للصوت يتميز بها عن صوت آخر مثله في الخفة والثقل

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r11.claim: Letters divide into vowels, called long and soft letters in grammar, and consonants, which comprise the rest.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r11.anchor: الحروف إما مصوتة وهي التي تسمى في النحو حروف المد واللين ولا يمكن الابتداء

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r12.claim: Some consonants—bāʾ, tāʾ, dāl, and ṭāʾ—cannot be prolonged and exist only at the instant between held and released breath; they are sound's beginnings, aptly called its edges.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r12.anchor: كالباء والتاء والدال والطاء وهي لا توجد إلا في الآن الذي هو آخر زمان حبس النفس وأول زمان إرساله

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r13.claim: Some apparently prolongable consonants, such as ḥāʾ and khāʾ, may really be successive instantaneous letters that sensation fails to distinguish.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r13.anchor: مثل الحاء والخاء فإن الظن أن هذه جاءت آنية متوالية كل واحد منها آني الوجود

RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r14.claim: Sīn and shīn are probably genuinely temporal: they are sound qualities that continue for as long as the sound itself.
RAZI-FULL:v1p35/r14.anchor: كالسين والشين فإنها هيئات عارضة للصوت مستمرة باستمراره

BURHAN:v4p187/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p187/r6.speaker: القاضي ابن الجويني
BURHAN:v4p187/r6.claim: Ibn al-Juwaynī thinks إذن أكرمك may take a nominative verb to mean “if you come to me, I will honor you,” with the omitted clause replaced by tanwīn.
BURHAN:v4p187/r6.anchor: وقال القاضي ابن الجويني وأنا أظن أنه يجوز أن تقول لمن قال أنا آتيك إذن أكرمك بالرفع

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r1.claim: A report may be an indispensable part of a sentence, such as a nominal predicate or a verb that completes the clause.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r1.anchor: ينقسم إلى خبر هو جزء من الجملة ، لا تتم الفائدة دونه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r2.claim: A circumstantial phrase also conveys a report, but attaches it secondarily to the main report and states the circumstance in which it occurs.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r2.anchor: فالتبس به الإثبات على سبيل التبع للمجيء ، وبشرط أن يكون في صلته

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r3.claim: A nominal predicate asserts an attribute without implying renewal, whereas a verb presents its meaning as recurring or newly occurring over time.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p140/r3.anchor: موضوع الاسم على أن يثبت به المعنى للشيء من غير أن يقتضي تجدده شيئا بعد شيء . وأما الفعل

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r1.claim: Reasoning does not determine which sounds burden the tongue; that judgment belongs to sensory perception.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r1.anchor: وليس الفكر الطريق إلى تمييز ما يثقل على اللسان مما لا يثقل ، إنما الطريق إلى ذلك الحس

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r2.claim: The Qur'an is miraculous as God's speech through the nazm it has, while nazm is unrelated to the taste or ease of individual letters.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r2.anchor: إنما كان قرآنا وكلام الله عز وجل بالنظم الذي هو عليه . ومعلوم أن ليس النظم من مذاقة الحروف

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r3.claim: Rational thinkers agree that the quality which makes the Qur'an reach a level beyond human capacity is eloquence and balāgha.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r3.anchor: اتفاق من العقلاء أن الوصف الذي به تناهى القرآن إلى حد عجز عنه المخلوقون هو الفصاحة والبلاغة

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r4.claim: If light, easy letters made speech eloquent, then vulgar low speech and bad verse would count as eloquent whenever their sounds were light.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r4.anchor: السوقي الساقط من الكلام ، والسفساف الرديء من الشعر فصيحا إذا خفت حروفه

JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r5.speaker: author
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r5.claim: If iʿjaz depended on ease of articulation, changing every ḍamma and kasra to fatḥa would preserve or increase it even when the meaning changed, an untenable result.
JURJANI-DALAIL:v1p377/r5.anchor: فجعل مكان كل ضمة وكسرة فتحة فقال : ' الحمد لله ' بفتح الدال واللام والهاء
